text:
maria-partners: Quick sync  we need a pricing guardrail for the next private-offer batch. Proposal: graduated thresholds that trigger customer-visible safeguards (alerts, 7-day grace, auto-topup opt-in).
tim-sales: +1. Use committed USD and token thresholds, not just SKU. Works better for appliance customers. :thumbsup:
anya-gtm: I'll draft two FAQs: marketplace listing + private-offer docs. Must include behavior at 80/100/120% and clear UI copy for auto-topup toggle.
noah-legal: Drafting opt-in language now. Recommend: auto-topup default OFF for private offers; 7-day grace; disputes for overage credit within 30 days.
ari-platform: On infra: we can emit webhooks at thresholds with payloads as simple strings. Also can enable model-variant fallback (quantized) when cost spikes, but partner must opt-in in offer metadata.
maria-partners: Suggest a minimum price anchor per hardware class to avoid listings that break renewal math. Also renewal discount ladder: Y1 20%, Y2 15%, Y3 10% to prevent permanent erosion.
tim-sales: That ladder helps renewals. I'll run scenario spreadsheet with metered->commit ramps and overage calc by EOD tomorrow.
anya-gtm: I will prepare the announcement blurb and partner-facing FAQ.
noah-legal: Also adding a "migration credit" clause if Redwood introduces model changes that materially change unit economics; will propose trigger language.
marketplace-bot: Validator note: include commit_terms and auto_topup fields in offer metadata.
maria-partners: Action items assigned. Reconvene after Tim's spreadsheet. Thanks. :pray:
